actions.name: Scan for poorly configured networking devices using SNMP
actions.description: The Russian FSB Center 16 cyber actors primarily use scanning to identify poorly configured networking devices, primarily routers, for exploitation. The actors scan for Internet IP ranges with active Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) agents that accept common or default community strings for authentication. These scans, run via proxies, consist of SNMP Set-Requests from a spoofed IP address containing Object Identifiers (OIDs) that instruct the SNMP agent on poorly configured networking devices.

actions.name: Copy router configuration to a file
actions.description: The actors instruct the SNMP agent on poorly configured networking devices to copy its configuration to a file, often called “config.bkp” or “output.txt”.

actions.name: Transfer configuration file to actor-controlled server
actions.description: The actors transfer the copied configuration file, typically using Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP), to an actor-controlled leased virtual private server (VPS) or compromised FTP server.

actions.name: Exploit common vulnerabilities and exposures (CVEs) in Cisco devices
actions.description: The actors occasionally exploit common vulnerabilities and exposures (CVEs) in Cisco devices, Cisco’s Smart Install (SMI) functionality, and web portals to manage network devices. The actors previously exploited at least CVE-2018-0171 and CVE-2008-4128.

relations.rationale: Copying the router configuration to a file depends on scanning to identify poorly configured devices
